issues.description: GetLimit mutates the shared *RateLimit and creates a throwaway stats counter on every request
issues.detail: The override branch reassigns Stats and FullKey on the *RateLimit returned from the descriptor tree, corrupting state across concurrent requests, and calls NewRateLimit/NewStats with the pre-enhancement key only to discard it. Sequential tests hide the race. Fix by returning a fresh RateLimit (or precomputing keys at load) and dropping the dead allocation.

issues.description: Three key-building branches collapse to a single predicate
issues.detail: matchedViaWildcard, matchedUsingValue, and the default arm each independently append entry.Key and conditionally append _value when valueToMetric is set. The cases reduce to: always write key; append _value iff (matchedUsingValue or (valueToMetric and value != "")). The duplication signals no stated invariant and makes the equivalence non-obvious.

issues.description: Hot-path string builder and stats lookup run unconditionally on every GetLimit call
issues.detail: valueToMetricFullKey is constructed for every request even when no descriptor in the matched chain enables value_to_metric, and the override-guard comparison uses a FullKey that is unset on the common path. Compute a chain-level boolean at load time and skip both the builder and the NewStats override entirely when it is false.

issues.description: detailed_metric and value_to_metric are one decision split into two booleans with implicit precedence
issues.detail: Both flags answer the same question: how should this descriptor render its metric segment (KeyOnly, KeyValue, Detailed)? Modeling them as two orthogonal booleans with a precedence rule documented in prose invites accretion and confusion. Collapse to a single per-descriptor MetricMode computed once at config load, then render from data.

issues.description: Positional struct literal for rateLimitDescriptor is fragile to field additions
issues.detail: Constructions like &rateLimitDescriptor{map[string]*rateLimitDescriptor{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric} rely on field order. Future flags (which this PR's pattern predicts) will silently shift meaning or force every call site to change. Use named-field initialization.

issues.description: Unbounded-cardinality stats creation has no operator guardrail
issues.detail: The feature is designed to inject runtime values into metric names, but there is no length cap, character sanitization, or creation-rate guard. An operator enabling value_to_metric on a high-cardinality key (subject_id, request_id) will allocate stats objects indefinitely. The README warning is informal; add a defensive bound or explicit configuration check.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a single verdict: the feature works in tests but the GetLimit hot path is unsound. The dominant defect is that the override branch mutates a shared *RateLimit from the descriptor tree and wastes a NewStats allocation on every request — a race the sequential tests cannot witness. Secondary issues are duplicated key-building branches that reduce to one predicate, unconditional per-request string and stats work that should be gated by a load-time flag, and a design choice that splits one metric-render decision across two booleans. Fix the aliasing first, collapse the formatting to one rule, and lift the override work to config load.
